content:
jess-support: FYI ACME doing a post-migration load test reported intermittent 429s + long tail latency. They say things look fine for ~10s then a bunch of requests either time out or come back 429.
acme-integ: Confirmed. This happens when we ramp from 50 -> 500 rps. A subset of completions (long context, chat) start returning 429s ~20s after ramp. Not every request, kind of bursty.
jess-support: Attached a couple of X-Request-Id logs and a snippet of headers: `X-Quota-Remaining: 3`, `X-Trace: trace-abc123`. Also they are using client-side batching + prefix prefetch enabled.
sanjay-runtime: Interesting. My first hypothesis: quota tokens exhausted because continuous batching is holding requests waiting on KV prefetch/warmup which increases perceived concurrency and eats burst quota.
acme-integ: What is "perceived concurrency"? Requests were queued on our side for ~60-120ms but server side delays look like 200-800ms before the 429s show up.
marta-sre: Perceived concurrency = number of in-flight logical requests that the platform counts while they sit in batching/queue. If a batch holds many logical requests waiting on KV (prefetch), the quota accounting can spike and hit burst limits, then subsequent requests get 429s even though CPU/GPU looks fine.
alex-devex: Can you repro? If so we can craft a short repro script and test mitigations (lower batch delay, disable prefetch, client backoff).
jess-support: ACME can repro in ~5-10 minutes with a local script. They provided steps: 1) send 50 warmup chat requests, 2) ramp to 500 rps for 30s, 3) keep long context (>2048 tokens) messages enabled, 4) enable client batching at 50ms and server-side KV prefetch on.
sanjay-runtime: Repro steps I use locally:```
# simple repro (python)
for i in range(600):
  send_request(concurrency=250, prompt=long_context)
  sleep(0.06)
```
You should see a cluster of 429s appear shortly after ramp if quota/batching are interacting.
eng-bot: [ops] Toggle `kv.prefetch.enabled=false` rolled to canary in us-west-2 (deploy id d-20250315).
marta-sre: Observed behavior when prefetch=true: KV prefetch spawns async warmups that block batch completion until prefetch resolves (implementation detail). That extends batch latency and holds logical slots -> quota burn.
acme-integ: If we turn off prefetch will latency go up? We want to avoid quality regressions.
sanjay-runtime: If prefetch is off, the first hit might be a cache miss causing a small extra latency on that request only. But it avoids holding many requests open waiting for prefetch, so overall tail latency and 429s improve. There's a tradeoff: slightly higher single-request latency for reduced cluster-wide contention.
alex-devex: Short-term mitigation options: 1) disable KV prefetch for this customer, 2) reduce client-side batch delay to 10-20ms, 3) add client-side jittered exponential backoff for 429, 4) temporarily increase burst quota for the org or migrate them to Dedicated.
jess-support: ACME tried reducing client batch delay to 20ms and saw fewer 429s but still spikes. They can test disabling prefetch next.
marta-sre: Longer-term runtime changes I recommend: a) avoid blocking batch completion on remote prefetch (return partial batch with placeholders), b) make quota accounting use effective concurrency (exclude queued-but-not-sent until kernel/kv ready), c) add a config knob for `batch.max_hold_ms`.
sanjay-runtime: Also watch for prefix starvation: heavy prefixes can cause hot-keying on KV which lengthens prefetch and amplifies the effect. If they use wide variety of prefixes it's less likely, but ACME uses a few heavy prefixes.
acme-integ: Any quick server-side tweak we can ask ops to try?
eng-bot: [ops request] Can we temporarily set `quota.burst_tokens` +50% for org:acme-inc for 2 hours?
marta-sre: I'll approve a short bump but we should pair it with disabling prefetch on their account first to prevent repeat. Requesting change now.
jess-support: I'll coordinate with ACME. Also adding recommended client retry: `retry-after` exponential backoff starting at 100ms, cap 2s, jitter.
sanjay-runtime: For the internal ticket, assign to eng-runtime to add a non-blocking prefetch path. I can sketch a patch: if prefetch takes longer than 12ms, return current batch without waiting and trigger async fill + KV cold-path for missing keys.
acme-integ: After ops bump + disabling prefetch we reran and 429s dropped to near zero; tail latency improved. We'll keep monitoring. Thanks! :tada:
marta-sre: Filing follow-up action items: 1) eng-runtime RFC for non-blocking prefetch, 2) product doc for recommended client batching settings, 3) ops procedure for temporary burst quota increases.
jess-support: Closing loop with ACME and will reopen if anything else crops up.
